critique: The matched Θ(n^{-1}) theorem is confined to fixed cumulant separation and treatment-code L1 error below the fixed threshold ε0; the contour bank, conditioning modulus, and risk constants can deteriorate without control as separation vanishes. It therefore does not determine the local-to-Gaussian minimax frontier, adaptive switching rule, uniform inference theory, or any class-wide local converse; the Gaussian–Rademacher result is only a path-specific upper bound. The result on the full Jin–Mackey–Syrgkanis ACE class is a class-minimax statement and does not establish that the published ACE estimator is suboptimal, so the estimator comparison remains upper-versus-upper. Represented-data computability is conditional on a still-unimplemented compiled interval-arithmetic substrate; only the ordinary-sample Borel estimator and its fixed-separation risk theorem are unconditional. The framing states these limitations consistently and does not present the open local frontier as settled.
